newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depos, swaps slightly lower in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek depos, swaps slightly lower in late trade.

text.p: Greek interbank deposits and long-term forex swaps were trading slightly lower and ecu/drachma was easier in late dealings on Tuesday, dealers said.
"Interbank deposits are trading slightly lower affected by fresh cuts in T-bill interest rates on Monday," said a dealer at BNP, Athens.
On Monday, the Greek finance ministry cut gross interest rates on three-, six- and 12-month T-bills by 40 basis points to 9.4, 9.7 and 10.5 percent respectively, effective February 24.
Six-, nine- and 12-month forex swap rates had also been influenced and were trading slightly lower in late dealings, he said.
"But the market is idling and we expect nothing exciting to happen in the next few sessions," he added.
The central bank kept its intervention rate in overnight money unchanged at 11.90 percent.
Ecu/drachma was trading slightly lower on small sales of ecus for drachmas.
"The market is quiet. Some sales of ecus for drachmas were observed as investors prefer to make the shift and gain from the interest rate differential", a forex dealer said.
Bonds were steady with no strong buying or selling interest, a state-bank bond dealer said.
The mark was quoted at 156.25/35 from Tuesday's 156.290 fix, the dollar at 261.60/70 drachmas from 261.840 and the Ecu at 303.40/50 from 303.520 drachmas.
